name: Fabric
description: Crowdsourced AI patterns you can pipe anything through: summarize a page, extract insights, or critique code without reinventing the prompt.
whyFound: 43k GitHub stars and still the cleanest way to reuse battle-tested prompts from the terminal. Homebrew packages it as fabric-ai.
beatsIncumbent: One-off ChatGPT tabs. You get named patterns instead of retyping the same prompt.

name: btop
description: A resource monitor that actually explains CPU, memory, disks, and network without looking like 1984.
whyFound: 34k stars and still the monitor 2026 roundups tell people to install instead of top. Open CLI already lists btm; btop is the one most humans actually want.
beatsIncumbent: top and htop. Same job, readable by default.

name: fx
description: Interactive JSON exploration in the terminal. Pipe API output in, fold it, and query it without writing a jq program first.
whyFound: 20k stars and the missing companion to jq: jq is for scripts, fx is for looking.
beatsIncumbent: jq when you do not yet know the shape of the JSON.

name: VHS
description: Record a terminal session from a tape file and get a GIF. Useful for CLI docs, READMEs, and showing an agent what a command looks like.
whyFound: Charm's recorder is the least painful way to document a CLI without opening a video editor. 20k stars, still maintained.

name: jqp
description: A TUI playground for jq. Tweak a filter against real JSON until it works, then paste the filter into a script or agent command.
whyFound: jq remains non-negotiable, but the filter language is the part people bounce off. jqp is the rehearsal room.
beatsIncumbent: Trial-and-error jq in a raw shell.
